paper_a.title: Moser-Tardos resampling algorithm, entropy compression method and the subset gas

paper_b.title: Entropy Compression Method and Legitimate Colorings in Projective Planes

metadata.description: Both papers operate within the Moser-Tardos / entropy-compression framework for the algorithmic Lovasz Local Lemma in the variable setting. Paper A (Fialho-Lima-Procacci) is a unification paper: it introduces the Forest-Algorithm and a single criterion (Theorem 2.1) that subsumes both the Pegden/Moser-Tardos LLL and the Alves-Procacci-Sanchis entropy-compression criterion via the subset gas. Paper B (Bissacot-Doin) is a representative application: it uses a variant of the Esperet-Parreau entropy-compression theorem to construct legitimate colorings of projective planes. The shared method (entropy compression / resampling on a variable setting with bad events) is the principal axis of overlap, while the goals differ (general criterion vs concrete bound).

matches.explanation: Paper A's explicit Dependency graph definition (graph $\GG$ on $\FF$ with the standard $\sigma$-algebra independence condition) has no explicit counterpart in paper B. Paper B operates in the variable-version setting where dependency is induced implicitly via shared variables in $\mathrm{vbl}(A_x)$ and never names a dependency graph.

Both define the variable setting of Moser-Tardos: a probability space generated by mutually independent discrete variables, together with a family of bad events (called 'tempered' / 'depending on subsets of variables'). Paper A names it 'Variable setting (Moser-Tardos)' and paper B calls it 'Variable version of the Lovasz Local Lemma setting'. Both cite Moser-Tardos 2010; both are external. Statements are notational paraphrases of the same object.

Paper A's uniform variable setting plus the seed/tidy/power machinery (Definitions 1.5 and Power) play the same role as paper B's bad-setting indexing data $(\mathcal{Z}, C_i, k_i, m_i, l_i, E, d_l)$: both encode the combinatorial weights ($d_s$ vs $d_l$, $k$ vs $m_i$) that the entropy-compression / forest-algorithm bound consumes. They are different formalisations of the same accounting (seed cardinality and number of extensions), so analogous rather than exact.

The general (non-uniform) seed and power definitions are paper A's contribution, used to state Theorem 2.1 outside the uniform setting. Paper B works exclusively in the uniform-projective-plane setting and never introduces a general seed.

The witness forest is the central combinatorial object of paper A's Forest-Algorithm analysis. Paper B's entropy-compression argument uses the register vector $R$ (DP418.4) instead of a forest construction, so there is no direct counterpart.
Admissible sequences are an internal device of paper A's S-Check argument. Paper B does not use this object.

Paper B's register vector $R = (\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ stores the entropy-compression history. Paper A bypasses the register-based information-theoretic argument in favor of a direct generating-function bound on witness forests, so no analogue appears.

The 'bad setting' as a (vertex subset, coloring) pair is paper B's framing; paper A speaks of bad events depending on $\psi_A$ which is structurally close (DP422.5) but not identical, so we leave bad setting unmatched and link DP418.3 to DP422.5 as the variable-version analogue.

Definitions specific to the projective-plane application: projective plane $P_n$, line types and legitimate colorings, dangerous pairs, optimal block size $\underline{m}$. None of these has a counterpart in paper A's general-theory development.

The classical Lovasz Local Lemma (Erdos-Lovasz) and its CELL improvement are cited only as background in paper A. Paper B's external citations (TP418.2, TP418.3, TP418.4) cover Esperet-Parreau, Alon-Furedi and McDiarmid; none of these correspond to LLL/CELL in the same role.
Fernandez-Procacci is a polymer-system / cluster-expansion result used in paper A's APS thread. Paper B has no polymer-side machinery.

Both are external prior-art results that paper-A and paper-B respectively generalise. TP422.4 (Pegden's algorithmic LLL with $\Xi_\ev$) is the algorithmic-LLL benchmark paper A's Theorem 2.1 strengthens; TP418.2 (Esperet-Parreau entropy compression) is the prior-art benchmark paper B's Theorem 1 modifies. They live in the same lineage (algorithmic LLL via resampling / entropy compression) but are formally distinct theorems, so analogous.

TP422.5 (Alves-Procacci-Sanchis 'entropy compression lemma') is the uniform-setting entropy-compression criterion that TP418.2 (Esperet-Parreau) seeded. Both state: in the uniform variable setting, a tidy-flaw growth condition implies existence of a good configuration found by entropy compression in linear expected time. Paper A reformulates the criterion via $\alpha$ and $d_s$; paper B keeps the Esperet-Parreau form and modifies it (RP418.1) to drop the $k_{(H,c)}$ constraint. Same theorem family, different cuts.

Both are the respective papers' main theorem and both upgrade an entropy-compression / Esperet-Parreau-style criterion. Paper A's TP422.6 (Forest-Algorithm criterion: $\min_\xi \phi_\FF(\xi)/\xi < 1$) is a unifying generalisation in the general variable setting; paper B's TP418.1 (variant of Esperet-Parreau giving an explicit color-count $\lceil \gamma \sup_i (d_{l_i} m_i)^{1/l_i} \rceil$) is a strengthening that removes the original second constraint of Esperet-Parreau. Both invoke a generating-function / characteristic-equation step ($\phi_E(\tau) - \tau\phi_E'(\tau) = 0$ in B mirrors $\rho = \min_\xi \phi_\FF(\xi)/\xi$ in A). They are not identical statements but are different formulations of the same SM technique.
Paper A's 'global subset gas' lemma (LP422.1) is its connection to the polymer / subset-gas viewpoint. Paper B has no polymer formulation.

Goodness preservation, phase-count and witness-tree structure are internal lemmas of the Forest-Algorithm analysis; paper B's entropy-compression analysis does not use phases or a witness-tree decomposition.

Both pairs are the workhorse 'compression / probability-bound' lemmas of the respective methods. Paper A's S-Check probability bound and witness-forest probability bound (LP422.5, LP422.6) bound the probability that an admissible sequence / witness forest is realised by the random execution. Paper B's Lemma 1 (uncolored set determined by register) and Lemma 2 (lossless reconstruction from register + final config) play the corresponding lossless-information-bookkeeping role inside the entropy-compression argument. Different formal devices (forest probability vs information-theoretic compression) executing the same analytical move, so analogous.

The classical Moser-Tardos resampling algorithm is cited as background in paper A. Paper B's algorithm AP418.1 is an entropy-compression-style backtracking algorithm that uncolors variables and records a register, not the plain Moser-Tardos resampling, so AP422.1 has no direct counterpart.

Both are entropy-compression backtracking algorithms in the Esperet-Parreau / Alves-Procacci-Sanchis lineage. AP422.2 (entropy compression in the uniform setting) and AP418.1 (modified Moser-Tardos / Esperet-Parreau algorithm) share: initialise variables to uncolored, color the smallest uncolored variable from a sample vector, on a flaw / bad setting uncolor a chosen subset and continue, halt when no flaw remains. AP418.1 additionally maintains a register vector $R$, which is the lossless-compression bookkeeping not explicit in AP422.2. Same algorithmic skeleton, slightly different bookkeeping.

Paper A's main contribution Forest-Algorithm (AP422.3) is a Moser-Tardos variant that preserves a seed during recursive resampling, used to prove the unifying TP422.6. Paper B's AP418.1 is the entropy-compression algorithm used to prove TP418.1. They are different algorithms (recursive seed-preserving resampling vs backtracking entropy-compression), but both are the algorithmic engine of their paper's main theorem and both descend from Moser-Tardos. Listed analogous to capture the SM relation.
S-Check is a validation / proof-only auxiliary algorithm specific to paper A's witness-forest analysis.

Application-side scaffolding for the projective-plane bound: the Fact 1 / Fact 2 propositions, the corollary on $|S|$, the Alon-Furedi and McDiarmid citations, the legitimate-coloring problem, the Alon-Furedi conjecture, and the constants $K, P_a, P_b$. Paper A is a method paper and contains no analogue.
Clique upper bound on $\Xi_\ev$ is a polymer-side estimate from BFPS; no counterpart in paper B.

Paper A's generating-function equation $W(z) = z\phi_\FF(W(z))$ and the coefficient bound $Q_n \leq \rho^n$ (with $\rho = \min_\xi \phi_\FF(\xi)/\xi$, via Flajolet-Sedgewick) are the analytic-combinatorics core of paper A's bound. Paper B uses the analogous algebraic step $\phi_E(\tau) - \tau\phi_E'(\tau) = 0$ inside the proof of TP418.1 / PrP418.3 (see PSP418.6) but does not extract it as a standalone equation node; we mark this analogous at low confidence as the underlying analytic move is the same characteristic equation, only emitted as an L1 node in A.

Remarks RP422.1 (LLL/APS correspondence) and RP422.2 (equivalence of Theorem 2.1 with the entropy-compression criterion) are paper A's unification commentary; paper B does not discuss the polymer connection.
Proofs of the Forest-Algorithm internal lemmas (goodness preservation, phase count, witness-tree structure) have no counterpart in paper B.

Both are the central probability / information-bookkeeping proofs of the respective methods. PP422.4-5 prove that the random execution producing an admissible sequence or witness forest is bounded by the product of event probabilities. PP418.1 proves Lemma 2 (lossless reconstruction of colors from $((R_j),\phi_i)$) by induction with the empty-vs-nonempty $R_i$ case split. Both establish the lossless / probability-bound that drives the main theorem; analogous.

Paper A's PP422.6 proves the main theorem TP422.6 by encoding runtime via witness forest, summing over forests, deriving the generating-function equation $W(z) = z\phi_\FF(W(z))$ and applying $\rho = \min_\xi \phi_\FF(\xi)/\xi$. Paper B's PP418.5 proves Proposition PrP418.3 by using Theorem 1's bound with the characteristic equation $\phi_E(\tau) - \tau\phi_E'(\tau) = 0$ giving $\tau = (\underline{m}-1)^{-1/\underline{m}}$. The analytic-combinatorics characteristic-equation step is the same; the surrounding scaffolding differs (forest-level proof vs application of an already-proved Theorem 1).
Proofs of the projective-plane Facts 1 / 2 and the |S| corollary are application-specific; no analogue in paper A.

Paper A's three example applications of Theorem 2.1 (nonrepetitive vertex coloring, facial Thue choice index of planar graphs, beta-frugal coloring) and paper B's projective-plane proposition PrP418.3 sit in the same role: each takes a Moser-Tardos / entropy-compression criterion off the shelf and instantiates it for a specific coloring problem to extract a numerical bound. Listed at low confidence because the underlying coloring problems are different and the match is structural-role, not statement-level.
